messages.author: 4ebc96d60052ef80
messages.subject: Plotting two different data frames
parts:
Dear All,

I suspect that this is straight forward, but I can't quite see how to
do it and the folks in the UK can't get the book for another week!

I have two data frames. The first I would to display on the graph as
points, e.g.

x=seq(1,10)
df1=data.frame(x, y=rnorm(10),experiment = rep(c(1,2),5))
m1 = ggplot(df1, aes(x=x,y=y,group=factor(experiment))) + geom_point
(aes(shape =factor(experiment)))

The second

x=seq(1,10,0.1)
df2=data.frame(x, y=rnorm(91))

I want to add to the plot as a line.

In traditional R speak, I have

plot(df1$x, df1$y)
lines(df2$x, df2$y)

Cheers

Colin

messages.author: 7e54aa65e5af5819
messages.subject: Re: Plotting two different data frames
parts:
Try this:

(m1 <- ggplot(df1, aes(x=x,y=y,group=factor(experiment))) +
geom_point (aes(shape =factor(experiment))) )
(m2 <- m1 + geom_line(data = df2, aes(x,y,group=NA)))

--
http://learnr.wordpress.com

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: Plotting two different data frames
parts:
Yea, learnr has the right idea.  The code below will help with the line as well as clears up the code a little...

df1$exp <- factor(df1$experiment)
ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y, group = exp), data = df1) +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = y), data = df2) +
  stat_function(aes(x = x), fun = function(x) 0*x, colour = 'red')

Hope it helps,
david.

messages.subject: Re: Plotting two different data frames
parts:
It looks like you do need to keep aes(x,y,group=NA) inside geom_line.
Also, the axis coloring can be achieved more clearly with
geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "red")
